shared_elements: single large standing figure in profile occupying the panel
bearded profile head with elaborate coiffure/headdress
long garment with fringed or pleated hem rendered as fine parallel lines
figure holding an implement in a raised/gripping hand
carried weapon-like or attribute object at the shoulder/back
detailed patterned textiles and jewellery (bracelet, armlet)
repeated petal/rosette-like decorative motifs as a field or border band
low-relief carving with profile head and legs, near-frontal shoulders
justification: Both show a single monumental profile-standing figure filling the panel, bearded, in a long fringed/pleated robe with bracelets and armlets, grasping an attribute in the raised hand with another object slung at the shoulder, and both include repeated rosette/petal ornament (as field filler in A, as a border band in B), with closely comparable low-relief conventions of profile head, near-frontal torso, striated hair and finely ruled drapery. The decisive difference is that A's figure is a bird-headed winged composite carrying a bucket amid a dense floral thicket, while B's is a wholly human figure with a tall headdress holding an upright spear against a plain ground.
